title: Permission + Telemetry Cutover: SAML Bridge, Dual-write Validation, and Admin Fallback Runbook
creator: Priya Raman
description: Runbook and engineering ticket to coordinate the final migration from RBAC v1 -> RBAC v2 for production accounts. Focus areas: (1) dual-write correctness and eventual consistency backfill, (2) SAML/SSO mapping bridge and admin controls preservation, (3) audit log retention/forwarding during cutover, (4) canary/cutover gating and customer communications. This ticket owns the pre-cutover automation, validation queries, and emergency rollback steps.
acceptance_criteria: 1) All production namespaces pass dual-write parity checks for a 24h canary window (0 mismatched permission checks observed for canary namespaces). 2) Backfill job completes for legacy permission artifacts with <0.01% diff vs snapshot baseline. 3) SAML attribute mapping remains stable for top 50 enterprise orgs; automated smoke SSO logins succeed. 4) Audit events are duplicated to both old and new pipelines with no loss for the migration window (verified by seq numbers). 5) Post-cutover quick health: auth error rate <= baseline + 0.1% and median auth latency within SLO.
tasks: Implement non-blocking dual-write hook (feature-flagged) and deploy to staging (PR #8230)
Create parity-checking job: sample every 2s for canary namespaces and record mismatches (db job: parity-checker v2)
Build backfill worker that supports idempotent upserts and resume tokens (backfill-runner v1)
Add SAML mapping bridge to map legacy role names -> v2 role IDs (saml-bridge service)
Wire audit-forwarder to both legacy kafka topic and new cloud log sink during migration window
Prepare canary namespace list and customer opt-in form for early cutover tests
Draft and schedule customer comms: pre-cutover notice, migration-day runbook, post-cutover validation checklist
checklist: Parity-checker stable for at least 48h on staging
Backfill dry-run completed on shadow dataset
SAML bridge mapping table reviewed by security and SSO team
Audit-forwarder tested end-to-end for seq continuity
Runbook doc published to Confluence and on-call paged with schedule
Comms templates approved by legal and customer success
rollout_plan: T-72h: Freeze RBAC schema migrations for new features
T-48h: Enable dual-write (non-blocking) behind FF for 5% internal traffic
T-24h: Expand dual-write to 30% traffic; run parity-checker and publish daily report
Cutover Day 0: Open customer migration window; enable audit-forwarder duplication for all orgs
Cutover Day 0+4h: Begin progressive backfill for high-priority org cohorts (by size and SLA)
Cutover Day 1-3: Monitor parity metrics and SSO login success rates; triage mismatches
Cutover Day 3: If parity <99.99% for canaries, pause and run targeted reconcile jobs
Cutover Day 7: If stable, enable single-write to RBAC v2 and deprecate legacy store after 30d grace
rollback_plan: If parity-checker reports persistent mismatches (>0.01% over 4h) or SSO failures for any canary org: 1) Flip feature-flag to disable dual-write (writes continue to legacy store only), 2) Rehydrate missing v2 permissions from last-good snapshot, 3) Notify on-call infra and CS with mitigation steps and re-open scheduled customer opt-out. Full rollback steps are enumerated in Confluence runbook link.
monitoring_playbook: Metrics to watch: parity_mismatch_rate, rbacv2_write_failures, saml_bridge_login_success, audit_forward_seq_gap
Automated alerts: parity_mismatch_rate > 0.005% sustained 30m -> P0 page
Sampling: store full event samples for first 72h after changing dual-write percentage
Post-migration: increase audit retention to 90d for migration traces
